# Vision Clipping

> Vision Clipping is a done-for-you clipping and content distribution agency. It turns long-form content into short-form clips and posts them every day across a network of TikTok, Instagram, YouTube and Facebook accounts that the client owns, run by its own team on dedicated devices, geo-targeted to the markets the client sells in, with click attribution on every post. A separate music offer places artists' songs into trending edit formats across pages Vision Clipping owns.

Key facts:
- Co-founders: Jaden Malcolm and Emrah Bayraktar. Co-founder Emrah Bayraktar has been featured in Forbes, The New York Times and NPR reporting on the clipping industry.
- Results: 3 billion+ views generated for clients.
- Clients include Red Bull, LEGO, FaZe Clan, SHEIN, WD-40, Iman Gadzhi, Luke Belmar, Russell Brunson; content cut for Sexyy Red, NLE Choppa, JoJo Siwa.
- Brand offer: One channel: $3,000/month (4 accounts, 120 posts a month, $400 one-time setup); Four channels (recommended): $12,000/month (16 accounts, 480 posts a month, $1,600 one-time setup). Three-month minimum.
- Music offer: Minimum: £1,000/month (90 posts a month, 1 song, 2 niches); Standard: £3,000/month (300 posts a month, 2 songs, 3 niches); Premium: £5,000/month (300 posts on Vision Clipping pages, 90 on the artist's own accounts, 3 accounts the artist owns); Elite: £10,000/month (450 posts on Vision Clipping pages, 270 on the artist's own accounts, 9 accounts the artist owns).
- What makes it different: Accounts are owned by the client, not rented from anonymous clippers. One team runs everything: strategy, cutting, posting and reporting. Geo-targeted distribution from devices in the client's market. Attribution on every post, so clips are judged on traffic and sales, not views alone.
- Book a call: https://vision-clipping.com/book/ · Music enquiries: https://vision-clipping.com/music/start/
- Structured facts: https://vision-clipping.com/facts.json · Full text with video transcripts: https://vision-clipping.com/llms-full.txt

# Detail

## How the brand offer works

- A channel is four accounts (Instagram, TikTok, Facebook, YouTube) created and owned by the client.
- Each channel posts 120 times a month; every post is checked by a manager before it goes out.
- Accounts run on dedicated devices set up in the client's target region, so views land in the countries the client sells to.
- Every post is a test of hook, format and call to action; winners are rolled out across all accounts.
- The client gets a dashboard with click attribution and keeps every account and follower.
- Guarantee: If the goal agreed on the strategy call is not hit within the first month, work continues free until the next billing cycle.

## How the music offer works

- Vision Clipping cuts edits that carry the artist's song in trending formats: football, news and culture, ranked formats, meme and dance comps, military and fight edits, basketball, pop culture.
- The edits go out across Instagram, TikTok and YouTube on a network of pages Vision Clipping owns and runs, linked to the song's sound so viewers can use it and find it on streaming.
- Premium and Elite also build dedicated accounts the artist owns.
- Get started: https://vision-clipping.com/music/start/

- Brands: Red Bull, LEGO, FaZe Clan, SHEIN, WD-40, Cricket District, Nonstop
- Founders: Iman Gadzhi, Luke Belmar, Russell Brunson

# Frequently asked questions

### How is this different from just hiring an editor?

An editor gives you a few posts a week. We give you a whole system: a trained team, the software and infrastructure to run accounts you own at scale, geo-targeted distribution into any market, and full attribution on what is working. One person can't do what a whole operation does, and you're not managing anyone. We handle all of it.

Source: https://vision-clipping.com/

### What's the difference between an internal partnership and a public clipping campaign?

A public clipping campaign pays a crowd of random creators per view, which invites botting and people gaming the system to pull money out of it. An internal partnership is the opposite: a lean dedicated team running accounts you own and keep, distributing your content into the exact regions you want, with full attribution and none of the games. You get ownership, control, and real distribution instead of bought numbers.

Source: https://vision-clipping.com/

### Are the views real?

Yes. We run every account ourselves on real devices, posting real content to real platforms. There's no bought engagement and no fake traffic, because everything comes from accounts we operate ourselves. What you see on your dashboard is genuine reach from real people.

Source: https://vision-clipping.com/

### What if my content doesn't perform?

We'll tell you honestly. If we don't think a piece of content is going to perform, we'll say so upfront, and often it's a case of creative direction: adjusting the hooks, angles, and formats before we scale it. We test across accounts, find what lands, and steer the creative until it works.

Source: https://vision-clipping.com/

### What do I actually need to provide?

Your existing content. That's it. YouTube videos, podcast recordings, webinar footage, whatever you already have. We handle the editing, the accounts, the posting, and the reporting. If you've got creative direction you want us to follow, send it over. Otherwise you don't do anything except check the numbers.

Source: https://vision-clipping.com/

### What does a content repurposing agency do?

It turns your existing long-form content (podcasts, videos, webinars) into short-form clips and distributes them across social platforms for you, handling the editing, the accounts, the posting cadence, and the reporting, so you get reach without running the operation yourself.

Source: https://vision-clipping.com/content-repurposing-agency/

### How much does content repurposing cost?

It varies with volume, platforms and markets. Freelance editors charge per clip; managed agencies typically run monthly retainers from around $2,000 to $15,000+, and premium done-for-you partnerships that run a dedicated team on owned accounts start around $10,000 per month.

Source: https://vision-clipping.com/content-repurposing-agency/

### What content can you repurpose?

Anything with distinct, self-contained moments: podcasts, YouTube videos, webinars, keynotes, livestreams and interviews. A good hour of long-form usually yields 10 to 30 usable short clips.

Source: https://vision-clipping.com/content-repurposing-agency/

### What is a podcast clipping service?

A service that turns your podcast episodes into short-form clips and distributes them across TikTok, Instagram Reels, YouTube Shorts and X. A done-for-you service like Vision Clipping also runs the accounts, posts on a cadence, and reports on what performed, you just send the episode.

Source: https://vision-clipping.com/podcast-clipping-service/

### How many clips can you get from one podcast episode?

A typical hour-long episode yields 10 to 30 usable clips, depending on how many distinct, self-contained moments it contains. The limit is the time to cut, caption, format and post them consistently, which is exactly what the service handles.

Source: https://vision-clipping.com/podcast-clipping-service/

### Do I keep the accounts and audience?

Yes. Vision Clipping distributes on accounts you own and keep, so the audience you build is yours, not borrowed reach on someone else's profiles.

Source: https://vision-clipping.com/podcast-clipping-service/

### How much does a clipping agency cost per month?

Monthly retainers commonly range from around $2,000 for a light freelance-style arrangement to $15,000 or more for a full managed team with owned accounts, geo-targeting and attribution. Premium partnerships that run a dedicated internal team typically start around $10,000 per month.

Source: https://vision-clipping.com/blog/how-much-does-a-clipping-agency-cost/

### Is it cheaper to hire a freelance editor than a clipping agency?

Per clip, yes, a freelancer might charge $15 to $150 per edit. But a freelancer only edits; they do not run accounts, post at scale across markets, or give you attribution. Once you add the accounts, posting, management and reporting yourself, the true cost of the do-it-yourself route is usually higher than a managed retainer.

Source: https://vision-clipping.com/blog/how-much-does-a-clipping-agency-cost/

### Why do pay-per-view clipping campaigns look so cheap?

Public pay-per-view campaigns pay a crowd of creators roughly $0.50 to $2 per 1,000 views. They look cheap because you only pay for views, but you do not own the accounts, and paying per view invites botting and gamed numbers. You are buying a metric, not a distribution asset.

Source: https://vision-clipping.com/blog/how-much-does-a-clipping-agency-cost/

### What makes a clipping agency the best for founders?

The best clipping agency for a founder runs accounts you own (not borrowed reach), produces real views from real devices rather than bought numbers, targets the specific markets you care about, and gives you attribution so you can see which clips drive results. Price matters, but ownership, real reach and attribution are what actually compound.

Source: https://vision-clipping.com/blog/how-to-choose-the-best-clipping-agency/

### What red flags should I avoid when choosing a clipping agency?

Watch for pay-per-view models that invite botting, agencies that keep ownership of the accounts, no attribution beyond screenshots of view counts, vague reporting, and pressure to buy on view volume alone. If they can't explain how you keep the audience or how they measure results, that's a red flag.

Source: https://vision-clipping.com/blog/how-to-choose-the-best-clipping-agency/

### Should I choose a clipping agency based on price?

No, choose on cost per real result and whether you own the channel at the end. A cheap provider with no attribution can cost more than a pricier one, because you can't tell what's working, so you can't cut what isn't. Compare the outcome, not the sticker price.

Source: https://vision-clipping.com/blog/how-to-choose-the-best-clipping-agency/

### Is a clipping agency better than hiring an editor?

It depends on your goal. An editor is better if you just need clips and are happy to run the accounts, posting and strategy yourself. A clipping agency is better if you want distribution as an outcome, a managed team running accounts you own, posting at scale across markets, with attribution, without doing the operations yourself.

Source: https://vision-clipping.com/blog/clipping-agency-vs-hiring-an-editor/

### How much does an editor cost compared to a clipping agency?

A freelance editor typically charges $15 to $150 per clip. A managed clipping agency runs roughly $2,000 to $15,000+ per month because it includes the accounts, posting, geo-targeting, management and reporting an editor doesn't. Per clip the editor is cheaper; per real result the agency is often cheaper once you count your own time.

Source: https://vision-clipping.com/blog/clipping-agency-vs-hiring-an-editor/

### Can I start with an editor and move to a clipping agency later?

Yes, and many founders do. Starting with an editor is a sensible way to test whether a channel works. Once it does and running it yourself becomes the bottleneck, moving to a managed agency lets you scale distribution without hiring and managing a team.

Source: https://vision-clipping.com/blog/clipping-agency-vs-hiring-an-editor/

### How do you repurpose long-form content into short clips?

Start from content you already have (a podcast, video or webinar), find the self-contained moments with a strong hook, cut each into a 20 to 60 second clip, add captions and format vertically for the platform, lead with the hook in the first three seconds, then post consistently across accounts and track what performs.

Source: https://vision-clipping.com/blog/how-to-repurpose-long-form-content/

### How many clips can you get from one long-form video?

A good hour of long-form content usually yields 10 to 30 usable short clips, depending on how many distinct moments and strong hooks it contains. The limit is rarely raw material; it is the time to cut, caption, format and post them all consistently.

Source: https://vision-clipping.com/blog/how-to-repurpose-long-form-content/

### What long-form content is best to repurpose?

Anything with distinct, self-contained moments: podcasts, interviews, webinars, keynotes, YouTube videos, live streams and Q&As. The best source content has clear opinions, stories or specific advice you can lift into a standalone clip that makes sense without the full context.

Source: https://vision-clipping.com/blog/how-to-repurpose-long-form-content/

### What is a founder brand?

A founder brand is the public reputation and audience a company's founder builds by sharing their thinking, story and expertise - usually through content. It compounds into trust, inbound leads, easier hiring and fundraising, because people buy from and back founders they already know.

Source: https://vision-clipping.com/blog/how-to-build-a-founder-brand/

### How do founders build a personal brand?

By consistently turning what they already know into content - long-form (podcasts, talks, videos) repurposed into short-form clips distributed across platforms - so their ideas reach far more people than their existing following. The hard part isn't ideas; it's consistent distribution, which is why many founders use a done-for-you team.

Source: https://vision-clipping.com/blog/how-to-build-a-founder-brand/

### How much time does building a founder brand take?

Creating takes as little as a few hours a month if you repurpose existing long-form instead of making new content daily. The distribution - editing, posting across accounts, tracking - is the time sink, and it's the part founders most often outsource so the brand grows without owning their calendar.

Source: https://vision-clipping.com/blog/how-to-build-a-founder-brand/

### What is thought leadership?

Thought leadership is the reputation you earn when your audience sees you as a trusted authority on a topic. In B2B it's built by consistently sharing genuine expertise - opinions, frameworks, lessons - through content that reaches the right people. It drives inbound, shortens sales cycles, and makes hiring and fundraising easier.

Source: https://vision-clipping.com/blog/thought-leadership-is-a-distribution-problem/

### How do you build thought leadership online?

By turning expertise you already have into content and distributing it widely: record long-form (podcasts, talks, videos), cut the best moments into short clips, and post them consistently across platforms. The ideas are usually already there - the work is packaging and distributing them at scale, which is why many leaders use a done-for-you team.

Source: https://vision-clipping.com/blog/thought-leadership-is-a-distribution-problem/

### Is thought leadership worth it for B2B?

Yes - it's one of the highest-ROI channels in B2B because buyers trust people over brands. A leader with a distributed voice generates inbound demand, lowers customer-acquisition cost, and compounds over time, unlike paid ads that stop the moment you stop paying.

Source: https://vision-clipping.com/blog/thought-leadership-is-a-distribution-problem/

### What is the clipping economy?

The clipping economy is the market for short clips cut from long-form content (podcasts, livestreams, interviews) and posted at scale across TikTok, Instagram Reels, YouTube Shorts and X. Clippers are often paid per view, and brands use it as a low-cost, native-looking distribution channel.

Source: https://vision-clipping.com/blog/the-clipping-economy-explained/

### How big is the clipping economy?

Writing on LinkedIn in 2026, Shira Lazar estimated the clipping economy at roughly a $3 billion industry, and it has been covered by NPR, Forbes and Yahoo Finance as a fast-growing marketing channel.

Source: https://vision-clipping.com/blog/the-clipping-economy-explained/

### Do brands actually get results from clipping?

Yes. Forbes reported that the AI startup Cluely hired over 700 clippers, generated 100 million views in weeks, and reached $7 million in annual recurring revenue. The economics are strong because clipping costs roughly $1 to $5 per thousand views, a fraction of traditional advertising.

Source: https://vision-clipping.com/blog/the-clipping-economy-explained/

### Is clipping a scam?

No. Clipping is a legitimate, fast-growing marketing channel covered by NPR, Forbes and Yahoo Finance, and used by real brands to generate real results. What deserves caution is the open pay-per-view version, where anonymous clippers are paid per view, which can invite botting and inflated numbers.

Source: https://vision-clipping.com/blog/is-clipping-a-scam/

### Why do people think clipping is a scam?

Because the open, per-view corner of the market rewards inflated view counts and middlemen rather than brands, as NPR reported. Paying per view is a direct incentive to game numbers, so bought-looking results are common. Managed clipping on owned accounts avoids this.

Source: https://vision-clipping.com/blog/is-clipping-a-scam/

### How do I avoid getting scammed with clipping?

Use a managed team on accounts you own, with real attribution, rather than an anonymous per-view marketplace. Ask any provider whether you own the accounts, whether the views come from real devices, and how they attribute results to specific clips.

Source: https://vision-clipping.com/blog/is-clipping-a-scam/

### Does clipping actually work?

Yes. The public numbers are strong: NPR reported a streamer whose clips average 700,000 views versus 33,000 on the livestream, and Forbes reported an AI startup that reached $7 million in annual recurring revenue after generating 100 million views through 700+ clippers. Clipping works best when it is consistent and run on owned accounts with attribution.

Source: https://vision-clipping.com/blog/does-clipping-work/

### How much reach can clipping generate?

A lot, and cheaply. Forbes put clipping at roughly $1 to $5 per thousand views and noted that a single $5,000 influencer post buys about the same reach as 500 individual clips. Individual clips regularly out-perform the long-form they came from.

Source: https://vision-clipping.com/blog/does-clipping-work/

### Why does some clipping fail to work?

Usually because it is a one-off, anonymous, per-view campaign with no account ownership and no attribution. Reach that you do not own and cannot measure is hard to turn into results. Consistent, managed distribution on owned accounts is what makes clipping pay off.

Source: https://vision-clipping.com/blog/does-clipping-work/

### Has Vision Clipping been featured in the press?

Vision Clipping co-founder Emrah Bayraktar has been featured in NPR, Forbes and Yahoo Finance and as a guest on the Russell Brunson Show, in coverage of the clipping economy. The distribution expertise that coverage documented is what now runs behind Vision Clipping.

Source: https://vision-clipping.com/blog/emrah-bayraktar-vision-clipping-press/

### What did Forbes say about Emrah Bayraktar?

Forbes wrote that Emrah Bayraktar has personally generated over 400 million views for brands including Andrew Tate, Iman Gadzhi and Luke Belmar, in its February 2026 report on clipping in fintech marketing.

Source: https://vision-clipping.com/blog/emrah-bayraktar-vision-clipping-press/

### Is Vision Clipping legitimate?

Yes. It is a managed clipping and distribution agency co-founded by an operator whose work has been documented by NPR, Forbes and Yahoo Finance, and it runs real accounts with real attribution rather than anonymous per-view campaigns.

Source: https://vision-clipping.com/blog/emrah-bayraktar-vision-clipping-press/

### What is content clipping?

Content clipping is cutting long-form content such as podcasts, videos and livestreams into short clips of about 20 to 60 seconds, then posting them across TikTok, Instagram Reels, YouTube Shorts and X to reach new audiences. One hour of long-form usually yields 10 to 30 clips.

Source: https://vision-clipping.com/blog/what-is-content-clipping/

### How does content clipping work?

You find the strongest self-contained moments in your long-form content, cut them tight, add captions, format vertically, lead with the hook in the first three seconds, and distribute consistently across accounts and platforms.

Source: https://vision-clipping.com/blog/what-is-content-clipping/

### Why do brands use content clipping?

Because clips out-reach the long-form they came from and cost little. NPR cited a streamer whose clips average 700,000 views versus 33,000 on the livestream, and clipping runs roughly $1 to $5 per thousand views, a fraction of traditional advertising.

Source: https://vision-clipping.com/blog/what-is-content-clipping/

### Is clipping expensive?

No, relative to the reach it buys. Per-view clipping runs roughly $0.50 to $25 per thousand views, and Forbes noted a $5,000 influencer post buys about the same reach as 500 individual clips. Managed done-for-you retainers run from about $2,000 to $15,000+ a month.

Source: https://vision-clipping.com/blog/is-clipping-expensive/

### How much does clipping cost per view?

Roughly $1 to $5 per thousand views according to Forbes, and $0.50 to $25 per thousand according to Yahoo Finance, depending on the niche. NPR cited examples from $0.50 per thousand up to $25 per thousand views.

Source: https://vision-clipping.com/blog/is-clipping-expensive/

### Is clipping cheaper than running ads?

Usually, yes. Forbes reported that clipping at $1 to $5 per thousand views costs a fraction of traditional digital advertising, which is a major reason fintech and crypto brands adopted it. The catch is that cheap views you do not own are not the same as results.

Source: https://vision-clipping.com/blog/is-clipping-expensive/

### How much does a clipping campaign cost?

Clipping campaigns are priced per view, roughly $0.50 to $25 per 1,000 views depending on the niche, so the total budget is what matters. Real campaigns typically run from around $5,000 into the tens of thousands, and one campaign NPR cited had a $70,000 budget.

Source: https://vision-clipping.com/blog/how-much-does-a-clipping-campaign-cost/

### How is a clipping campaign priced?

Almost always per thousand views. You set a total budget and a per-view rate, and the campaign buys views until the budget is spent. Forbes put brand rates at about $1 to $5 per thousand views.

Source: https://vision-clipping.com/blog/how-much-does-a-clipping-campaign-cost/

### Is a cheap clipping campaign worth it?

Not always. A low per-view price often hides botted views, no account ownership and no attribution, so cheap reach you cannot measure or keep rarely turns into results. Judge on cost per real result, not the per-view sticker.

Source: https://vision-clipping.com/blog/how-much-does-a-clipping-campaign-cost/

### What is the difference between a mass and an internal clipping campaign?

A mass campaign pays a crowd of independent creators per view on their own accounts, which is cheap and fast but borrowed and easy to game. An internal campaign runs a managed team on accounts you own, into chosen markets, with attribution, which costs more per view but builds an asset you keep.

Source: https://vision-clipping.com/blog/mass-clipping-campaign-vs-internal-clipping-campaign/

### Which is cheaper, mass or internal clipping?

Mass is cheaper per view, often just $0.50 to $5 per thousand. Internal usually costs more per view but tends to cost less per real result, because the reach is targeted, owned and measured rather than anonymous.

Source: https://vision-clipping.com/blog/mass-clipping-campaign-vs-internal-clipping-campaign/

### Can you combine mass reach with internal control?

Yes. A managed operation on owned accounts can run at mass-campaign volume while keeping the control, geo-targeting and attribution of an internal team. That is the model Vision Clipping uses.

Source: https://vision-clipping.com/blog/mass-clipping-campaign-vs-internal-clipping-campaign/

### Should I build a clipping team in-house?

In-house is the right call when distribution is a core growth lever and you want to own the accounts, control quality and target specific markets. The trade-off is cost and management: a real in-house team runs roughly $10,000 to $30,000+ a month once salaries, tools and your time are counted.

Source: https://vision-clipping.com/blog/why-build-your-clipping-team-in-house/

### How much does an in-house clipping team cost?

Roughly $10,000 to $30,000 or more per month all in, covering editors, a manager, devices, software and management time. That is often more than a managed agency retainer, with the hiring risk on you.

Source: https://vision-clipping.com/blog/why-build-your-clipping-team-in-house/

### Is it better to build clipping in-house or use an agency?

Both give you ownership if done right. Pure in-house gives maximum control but carries hiring and management overhead. A managed agency like Vision Clipping runs the in-house model for you, on accounts you own, without you staffing it.

Source: https://vision-clipping.com/blog/why-build-your-clipping-team-in-house/

### Should you do mass clipping?

Yes, when you need cheap reach fast, for a launch, a drop or an awareness spike. Mass clipping runs about $1 to $5 per thousand views and can generate enormous reach quickly. It is less suited to building an audience you own long term.

Source: https://vision-clipping.com/blog/why-you-should-do-mass-clipping/

### Does mass clipping work?

It can work very well. Forbes reported a startup that generated 100 million views in weeks and reached $7 million in annual recurring revenue through clippers. The key is running it on real accounts rather than an anonymous per-view crowd.

Source: https://vision-clipping.com/blog/why-you-should-do-mass-clipping/

### How do you do mass clipping without getting botted?

Run it on real accounts you own, on real devices, with attribution, rather than paying an anonymous crowd purely per view. Paying per view is the incentive that invites botting; owned, managed distribution removes it.

Source: https://vision-clipping.com/blog/why-you-should-do-mass-clipping/

### Is clipping a form of manipulation?

Clipping is a distribution format, not manipulation in itself. The concern Le Monde raised is about anonymous, covert distribution that hides who is behind a message. Clipping done transparently for a real brand on accounts it owns is ordinary marketing, not manipulation.

Source: https://vision-clipping.com/blog/is-clipping-mass-manipulation/

### What did Le Monde say about clipping?

In a July 2026 investigation, Le Monde described clipping as the internet's new weapon of mass manipulation, reporting that AI tools can turn one thirty-minute video into up to 500 clips, and quoting a French clipping-agency founder on its power.

Source: https://vision-clipping.com/blog/is-clipping-mass-manipulation/

### Is clipping legitimate for brands?

Yes. Used with owned accounts, human editors and transparent attribution, clipping is a legitimate distribution channel. Its power, documented by NPR, Forbes and now Le Monde, is exactly why brands invest in it.

Source: https://vision-clipping.com/blog/is-clipping-mass-manipulation/

### Does Iman Gadzhi pay clippers?

Yes. Iman Gadzhi runs an official paid clipping campaign on Whop, the creator marketplace he co-owns, paying up to $2,000 for a single clip cut from his content. It sits alongside a large ecosystem of owned repurposing accounts and fan-run clip pages.

Source: https://vision-clipping.com/breakdowns/iman-gadzhi-clipping/

### What is a clipping operation?

A clipping operation is a system that turns long-form content, such as YouTube videos, podcasts and livestreams, into a constant stream of short clips distributed across TikTok, Instagram Reels and YouTube Shorts, using owned accounts, fan pages and paid freelance clippers.

Source: https://vision-clipping.com/breakdowns/iman-gadzhi-clipping/

### How is managed clipping different from marketplace clipping?

Marketplace clipping pays an open crowd of anonymous clippers per view, which gives you volume but no control over accounts, markets or message. Managed clipping runs distribution on accounts you own, into markets you choose, with attribution on what actually converted, which is how Vision Clipping operates.

Source: https://vision-clipping.com/breakdowns/iman-gadzhi-clipping/

### Does Luke Belmar have a YouTube channel?

Yes, but it is effectively dormant: about 450,000 subscribers, only ten videos ever uploaded, and nothing new since September 2023. Single podcast appearances about him now out-view his entire channel catalogue, and his reach is carried by third-party shows and fan-run clip pages.

Source: https://vision-clipping.com/breakdowns/luke-belmar-clipping/

### How did Capital Club grow so fast?

Through clip-driven distribution rather than owned posting. Whop's own blog credits Belmar with using its clipping system to blow up his personal brand for the Capital Club launch, and Vision Clipping's public case study reports 200M+ views on two owned pages driving $19M in Capital Club subscriptions.

Source: https://vision-clipping.com/breakdowns/luke-belmar-clipping/

### Who runs the Luke Belmar clip pages?

Mostly fans and anonymous operators. The largest archive channel has close to 100,000 subscribers and over a thousand videos, and the biggest Instagram fan pages appear to rival his own account's following. Almost none of them are verifiably operated by Belmar, which is exactly the trade-off of a fully rented audience.

Source: https://vision-clipping.com/breakdowns/luke-belmar-clipping/

### Did Polymarket pay TikTok creators for views?

Yes. NPR reported a Polymarket clipper campaign paying $0.50 per 1,000 views with a $70,000 budget, and a 2026 consumer-protection lawsuit describes marketplace bounties of $1 per 1,000 views. A Wall Street Journal analysis found the resulting videos drew more than 140 million views.

Source: https://vision-clipping.com/breakdowns/polymarket-clipping/

### Is paying clippers illegal?

Paying for clips is legal. The problems documented around prediction-market campaigns were deception and disclosure: videos depicting fake winnings and paid promotion that was not labelled as advertising. That is what drew the WSJ analysis, a consumer-protection lawsuit and senators' letters, not the act of paying for distribution.

Source: https://vision-clipping.com/breakdowns/polymarket-clipping/

### What is the alternative to per-view clipper campaigns?

Managed clipping: a private team distributing real content on accounts the brand owns, into chosen markets, with attribution on what converted. It removes the incentive to fabricate because nobody is paid per raw view. That controlled model is what Vision Clipping operates.

Source: https://vision-clipping.com/breakdowns/polymarket-clipping/

### Do music labels pay TikTok creators to promote songs?

Yes, extensively. NPR interviewed five music influencers who admitted taking label payments of $150 to $600 per post without disclosure, and Billboard's reporting put rates from $25 for micro-creators to about $10,000 for top creators. One major-label marketer estimated 75% of popular TikTok songs started as paid creator campaigns.

Source: https://vision-clipping.com/breakdowns/music-clipping/

### Do paid song promotions have to be disclosed?

The FTC requires disclosure of any material connection, in the video itself. But an FTC representative has suggested a song merely playing in a video's background, with no claims made about it, may not require disclosure. That gray zone is why undisclosed music promo persists, though creators who verbally hype a song for money are firmly inside normal endorsement rules.

Source: https://vision-clipping.com/breakdowns/music-clipping/

### How can an artist run clipping without losing control?

Run it as a managed operation: a private team cutting and posting the artist's content on pages the artist owns, aimed at the fanbases and markets that matter, with attribution on what actually converts to saves and streams. The reach compounds on assets the artist keeps, instead of renting burner accounts.

Source: https://vision-clipping.com/breakdowns/music-clipping/

### How does Diary of a CEO test its clips and thumbnails?

Steven Bartlett flags strong moments on a trackpad while recording, his team turns the best lines into titles and thumbnails, and they are tested as Facebook ads before launch, a method Bartlett says lifted click-through from about 2% to 20%. Episodes are also pre-tested with thousands of viewers, including eye-movement tracking, and the team has described running over 150 experiments in a single quarter.

Source: https://vision-clipping.com/breakdowns/diary-of-a-ceo-clipping/

### How many clips does Diary of a CEO post?

DOAC runs a dedicated clips channel publishing one 10-to-30-minute clip per day, plus a separate shorts channel and platform-specific cutdowns. Notably, the team tested doubling to two clips a day and reach went down, so they killed the experiment. No official clips-per-episode count is published.

Source: https://vision-clipping.com/breakdowns/diary-of-a-ceo-clipping/

### Can a smaller podcast copy the DOAC playbook?

The principles copy: treat clips as the discovery engine, test before you publish, own the channels the clips live on, and measure what converts listeners rather than what merely gets views. What does not copy easily is the 150-person operation behind it, which is the gap a managed clipping team fills.

Source: https://vision-clipping.com/breakdowns/diary-of-a-ceo-clipping/

### How do you make clips like Diary of a CEO?

Flag the strongest moments while recording, cut them into clips built around one hook, test titles and thumbnails before publishing, post daily to dedicated channels you own, and keep only what the retention data supports. DOAC layers a 150-person operation on that loop; a managed clipping team gives smaller shows the same system without the headcount.

Source: https://vision-clipping.com/breakdowns/diary-of-a-ceo-clipping/

### What share of Joe Rogan's views come from clips?

By the official channels' own lifetime numbers, the dedicated JRE Clips channel holds about 6.07 billion views against 6.64 billion on the main PowerfulJRE channel, meaning roughly half of all official JRE YouTube views ever have come from the clips channel alone, before counting clips posted on the main channel.

Source: https://vision-clipping.com/breakdowns/joe-rogan-clips/

### Why did Joe Rogan's clips stay on YouTube during the Spotify exclusive?

Because clips are the discovery engine. Announcing the 2020 exclusive, Rogan said: 'We will still have clips up on YouTube but full versions of the show will only be on Spotify after the end of the year.' Even a nine-figure exclusivity deal deliberately left the clips outside it.

Source: https://vision-clipping.com/breakdowns/joe-rogan-clips/

### How big was the Joe Rogan Trump episode?

The October 2024 Trump interview did 26 million YouTube views in its first 24 hours, 38 million within four days, and sits above 62 million today. At around 33 million views it had already exceeded the combined average prime-time audiences of ABC, NBC, CBS, Fox News, MSNBC and CNN.

Source: https://vision-clipping.com/breakdowns/joe-rogan-clips/

### How does Stake advertise if gambling ads are restricted?

By building distribution it does not have to buy: its founders launched the streaming platform Kick after Twitch banned Stake, it signs star deals reported in the nine figures, and clipper networks repost stream highlights to fan accounts for as little as two cents per thousand views, reaching feeds that gambling advertising cannot legally buy.

Source: https://vision-clipping.com/breakdowns/stake-clipping/

### Did Stake really pay Drake $100 million?

The partnership has been reported at $100 million, with accounts differing on structure: Forbes lists it as a $100 million deal from 2022, while later reporting described up to $100 million a year largely in gambling credit for livestreaming his sessions. Bloomberg later found his big-win rate on Stake's in-house games was roughly four times the average, findings Stake called categorically incorrect.

Source: https://vision-clipping.com/breakdowns/stake-clipping/

### Are the gambling wins shown in clips real money?

Often unclear, which is the industry's core disclosure problem. Reporting on Bloomberg's investigation notes streamers often gamble with funds provided by Stake itself, and a Kalshi clipping operation was found instructing clippers to simulate market screenshots. What is on screen is not necessarily anyone's money at risk.

Source: https://vision-clipping.com/breakdowns/stake-clipping/

### What is music clipping?

Music clipping is putting a song under short edits, such as football edits, culture recaps, ranked lists and dance comps, and posting them across many TikTok, Instagram and YouTube pages so viewers keep hearing the track and start using the sound.

Source: https://vision-clipping.com/music/guides/what-is-music-clipping/

### Is music clipping the same as paying influencers?

No. Paying an influencer buys one post from one creator. Clipping puts the song under many edits across many pages, every day, so it builds through repetition rather than a single moment.
